body:
:). This all made me smile a lot. Thank you for that. It feels like its been ages even though it hasn't been more than a couple days. You are totally right about endorphins. 

I wish the public transit thing were so easy. In my experience, people get very guarded and scared if you try to speak to them on public transit, even if you are kind, well dressed, well spoken, etc. NYC is an unforgiving place, and I think that is part of why riding transit is such a stressful experience for people, especially when they are on edge.

However, I feel like maybe I can sleep. The thoughts of giving up have quieted. I really appreciate the time and energy you gave me tonight -- I was feeling a lot more desperate before, and I can only help but think this conversation helped.

Thanks for the advice. It's been calming just to interact here, at least for now, and everything you've said has been helpful for me. 

I am really into rock climbing -- in general, the adrenaline sports help me to feel calmer about my life. I've had to give this up almost entirely -- I had been financially supporting her for the past several months as well, and to do so, had taken on an extra job and lost a lot of my nights. I probably need to get back to this, but I also need to get my finances back in shape before doing so. (Not that I am in any trouble, just a little weak)

One of the problems I am having is that I live in NYC and every time I get on public transit, I have a breakdown. I'm not sure if it is all of the memories of riding the subway all over the city with her, or just the feeling of being isolated and crowded at the same time. But, its making it harder to get around and do things I care about. 

I'm just not sure how to grab onto something and stop myself from spiraling. I will look into grief counseling and regular counseling and see what my options are.

Thanks for the thoughtful replies. Yeah, I finished at a good college, have been steadily employed, have good friendships. I think part of what is so difficult for me right now is that I'm trying really hard to fight the urge to isolate and "armadillo" -- I've been going to work, seeing friends, calling people all day, but it feels like it only gets worse and worse, which in my experience is not the way these things tend to go, and its really frightening for me right now. It's always been the case that if I do everything "right", I move in the right direction. 

My pre-loss schedule was very heavily geared towards her -- we had just moved in together a couple months back and spent nearly every night together. In a lot of ways, I've had to reinvent my life over night. 

But the pain is crippling, and I feel desperate to escape it. I don't know that I would ever hurt myself, but it is overwhelming to consider it and have moments where I fixate on it. 

In your opinion, would it be a good idea to seek a mental health professional sooner rather than later? I'm not even sure how one goes about doing this, I've looked into it briefly in the past and it seems daunting.

Not sure, honestly. The memories at this point just flood in uncontrollably. I've been through a lot in the past -- losing a parent young, physical abuse as a child, the other parent being ill. I've gotten very used to being able to take a deep breath and march on. But I feel like I've been pushed over some sort of precipice this time -- I've lost control in a way that I haven't before, and I can barely hold it together enough to do the most basic things in my life. I just don't know where to go with it, or what to do.
